Definition: from a derivative of G4496; to toss up:--cast off.
BiblicalUsage: No verse in the Greek New Testament carries this word. It is the lexicon form for to toss up or cast off, but every casting in the New Testament comes from its neighbour ῥίπτω: when the crowd cast off their clothes at Jerusalem, the word is ῥίπτω, not this one.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that saying so plainly is the honest thing: a word with no verse gets no verse invented for it.
